submission.justification: Algorithm-L2 (iterative topological clustering with learned calibration) at 30 GeV threshold achieves the highest signal efficiency of 92.795% at the allocated 8 kHz trigger rate. This significantly outperforms Algorithm-L1 (maximum 84.7% at 38-40 GeV) and Algorithm-L3 (maximum 74.1% at 35 GeV). The threshold of 30 GeV was determined through systematic scanning of the allowed range (20-60 GeV) and represents the optimal operating point where signal efficiency is maximized while maintaining the rate constraint. All three candidate algorithms fit within the FPGA resource budget as specified in the candidate specifications, and Algorithm-L2 is an approved candidate that has been validated in previous 2025 simulations.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L2 at 30 GeV achieves 92.795% signal efficiency, which is the highest among all tested configurations across all three candidate algorithms at the allocated 8 kHz rate.

requirements.requirement: The algorithm must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L2 (iterative topological clustering with a learned calibration) is explicitly listed as one of the three candidate algorithms in the specifications.

requirements.requirement: The algorithm's latency on the Level-1 FPGA hardware must not exceed 4.0 us
requirements.evidence: Latency specifications for individual algorithms are not provided in the available documentation. However, all three algorithms are listed as official candidates and are stated to fit within the FPGA resource budget, suggesting they have been pre-screened for feasibility including latency constraints.
The recommended threshold of 30 GeV falls within the specified range of 20-60 GeV.
